items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: And there I was, 23 years old and brand new in the business, and Milt Hinton, Osie Johnson, Dick Hyman, full string section, Doc Severinsen on trumpet.

ctx.x: But the best thing that happened on something that wasn’t one of those, I was at Dick Charles’ studio. And he called me up and said, “I think there’s an elderly man who’s written a lot of music for the Kraft Music Hall themes and stuff, Vladimir Solinsky. And

he has some songs he’s had lyrics put to and I think you’re the right singer to do it. And so I did and they were beautiful but not hip type songs. They were beautiful songs. And about two months later I got a call from the studio and they said, “Call Joe Reisman over at Roulette Records, he wants to talk to you.” And that’s where my album, the first one, “Born to be Blue” came, because he had an idea or he had a song that he wanted to use as the title song. Actually that was “Lonelyville.” And we did the whole…
What a business. Speaking of writing lyrics, I’m going to read — this is an excerpt from an Anne Phillips lyric and you have to finish it. Okay? “But no matter how I have tried, this feeling inside —
